distinguishing_features: Direct modulation of spindle speed based on tension to control slip velocity
Active prevention of thermal runaway by dynamically bounding heat generation
Use of inverse-sqrt relationship between tension and speed to maintain constant heat generation
Real-time pressure-driven speed control without altering mechanical components at the traveler-ring interface
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing excessive heat buildup in the traveler during high-speed ring spinning that leads to yarn breakage, without relying on hardware modifications or material changes
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism uses existing sensors and drives with a physically sound control law derived from the quadratic dependence of frictional heat on velocity, making it feasible at industrial scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The application of dynamic spindle speed modulation via tension feedback to directly bound heat generation is not an obvious extension of prior art that infers degradation from current or temperature, as it actively prevents failure through real-time energy management rather than merely predicting it.
